disposition_reason: Retain Pending and BLOCKED. Parameterization is valid only after purpose, method and safety boundary exist; here the missing information determines the testcase itself. `DF Common Options` can denote unrelated address-map, interleave, link, memory, policy, performance or RAS controls whose observation, mutation, activation and recovery differ materially. ED-11 prohibits choosing all/random or an arbitrary setting, and no authoritative platform/AGESA specification in the source selects one. A safe generic wrapper can state what a future definition must contain, but it cannot supply a DUT command or PASS/FAIL oracle. The BIOS/platform owner must provide a versioned completed contract; that new evidence then triggers a fresh independent review rather than automatic execution.
decision_basis: The exact XLSX row 1575, same-row tests.json/DeepSeek, exact GPT V2, historical V3.1 BLOCKED record, duplicate-code search and locked queue were read directly. The true next formal identity is physical row 1576 / variant 741aefaadaac80fa, a separate Memory Addressing testcase.
Both authoritative action-bearing cells are `TBD`. This is not a conflict between two usable methods and not a missing runtime IP/version/value; no executable semantic contract exists.

The label does not identify whether the test is menu visibility, default-value inspection, one reversible setting/persistence transition or functional validation. Each would require different evidence and classification.

No named setting or supported value matrix exists. ED-11 explicitly prohibits all/random BIOS mutation and permits only one safe reversible approved setting at a time; selecting a likely DF option would invent coverage.

No Expected Result exists. A screenshot showing the page, a generic setup dump or a successful command cannot create PASS/FAIL because correctness, supported state, activation and any workload effect are undefined.

No safety/recovery semantics exist. Some DF controls can affect socket/interconnect, memory mapping/interleave, bootability, performance or RAS, so a generic defaults reset or guessed rollback is unsafe and may not restore the Project recipe.

Public AMD terminology cannot repair the row without exact CPU family, board, BIOS/AGESA build and exposed option. OEM menu names and behavior can vary, and authoritative Project/OEM scope is indispensable.
The source's generic log clearing cannot be executed while blocked; it would destroy evidence without any approved action interval or event oracle.

An unblock definition must name one exact objective and checkpoint, platform/build, interface/path, read/write semantics, supported values, baseline/test/final state, activation/reboot requirements, expected result, evidence, approval, aborts and recovery. If multiple controls are intended, each needs separately identifiable coverage.

ED-02/ED-21 preserve this row apart from nearby cases; ED-03 does not permit guessing OEM semantics; ED-11 prohibits arbitrary all/random settings; ED-13/ED-14 require separate approval and safety; ED-15 prevents false N/A; ED-24 distinguishes Project recipe from factory default; ED-26 prohibits retry; ED-33/ED-35 preserve TBD history; ED-36 says core semantic absence can remain blocked; ED-38 prohibits DUT action/verdict.
